tagline: Car-free icon — every arrival is a boat arrival.
summary: Koh Phi Phi is a wholly car-free archipelago where Tonsai Pier is the single gateway and every internal and inter-island movement happens by water. It draws roughly 1.5 million visitors a year, with marquee global brand recognition anchored by Maya Bay — now so carefully managed that the national park caps entry at 4,125 visitors a day. With zero road competition and tightening conservation rules, Phi Phi is a near-pure fit for a quiet, zero-wake electric shuttle: it serves the concentrated gateway transfers from Phuket, Krabi and Ao Nang, the premium north-island resort runs to Laem Tong, and the low-wake park tours where diesel boats increasingly clash with the protected-water brand.

use_cases.title: Phuket / Krabi ↔ Tonsai gateway transfer
use_cases.body: A direct foiling crossing from the Andaman mainland to Tonsai, the island's single gateway, that flies above the open-water chop and lands guests fresh. It replaces a rattling diesel speedboat with the calm, premium start of a Phi Phi trip.

use_cases.title: Tonsai ↔ Laem Tong resort shuttle
use_cases.body: A smooth, near-silent foiling hop up to the north-island resorts at Laem Tong, reachable only by water. For high-value guests it turns the final leg into a signature arrival rather than a wet transfer.

use_cases.title: Low-wake national-park tours
use_cases.body: A zero-wake electric craft for Maya Bay and the surrounding national-park waters, where entry is capped and reef protection is paramount. The quiet, low-wash ride aligns directly with the conservation rules that diesel tour boats keep running up against.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Phi Phi pairs an ultra-short captive resort hop with mid-range gateway corridors that all sit inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — Tonsai↔Laem Tong (~4 nm), Phuket↔Tonsai (~24 nm) and Krabi↔Tonsai (~23 nm) — while the car-free island removes all road-modal competition and the single Tonsai gateway concentrates demand for easy shore-charging siting.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range, with no charging-infrastructure dependency, extends the network along the wider Andaman coast — Phuket, Krabi, Koh Lanta and the outer islands — bridging open-water legs that the car-free island's limited grid power could not support for all-electric charging.

competitive_landscape: Lomprayah, Tigerline, speedboat charters from Phuket/Krabi; longtails internally. All diesel; national-park noise/wake scrutiny rising — opening for electric.
seasonality: Peak: Nov-Apr. SW monsoon May-Oct raises Andaman swell and periodically closes Maya Bay; range-gate cross-corridors, keep Tonsai-Laem Tong hop year-round.
regulatory_note: Thai cabotage + Hat Noppharat Thara–Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park rules (Maya Bay access caps, low-wake favorability). Marine Department licensing; local partner-of-record advised.
